name: Natural Killer (NK)-Cell Enteropathy
aliases: NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract

criteria.description: Presence of atypical NK-cell infiltrate in the gastrointestinal mucosa without evidence of aggressive lymphoma
NK cells positive for CD56, CD3ε cytoplasmic, and negative for T-cell receptor gene rearrangement
Indolent clinical course without systemic symptoms or progression to lymphoma
Exclusion of NK/T-cell lymphoma and other malignant lymphoproliferative disorders by clinical, histologic, and molecular studies
Endoscopic evidence of mucosal abnormalities such as erythema, erosions, or ulcers in the gastrointestinal tract

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of atypical NK-cell infiltrate with characteristic immunophenotype, indolent clinical course, and exclusion of lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies to exclude T-cell receptor gene rearrangement are critical to differentiate from malignant NK/T-cell lymphoma.

laboratory: Normal peripheral blood counts or mild anemia
Absence of clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement
imaging: Endoscopic visualization of mucosal erythema, erosions, or ulcers
CT scan may show mild bowel wall thickening without mass lesions
genetic: Polyclonal NK-cell population confirmed by molecular studies
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD56, cytoplasmic CD3ε, granzyme B
Negative for CD5, CD8, and T-cell receptor rearrangement

distinguishingFeatures: Aggressive clinical course with systemic symptoms
Mass lesions or destructive ulcers on imaging
Chronic relapsing course with granulomas (Crohn's disease)

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Presence of mass lesions or lymphadenopathy on imaging
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Feldman AL, et al. NK-cell enteropathy: a benign NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder mimicking lymphoma. Blood. 2011;118(15): 4127-4134.
Jaffe ES. The 2016 revision of the WHO classification of lymphoid neoplasms. Blood. 2016;127(20):2375-2390.
